summary: The design is viable, but its approval, snapshot, target-resolution, schema-evolution, and trust contracts are not yet implementable from the current APIs. The largest risk is treating per-page CAS plus structural blast-radius queries as a complete, atomic audit inventory when both are explicitly weaker today.

suggestions.title: Define a real consistent decision inventory snapshot
suggestions.rationale: `DecisionRepository.inventory()` performs `list_pages()` followed by independent `get_page()` calls, skips pages deleted between those calls, and records decode failures as diagnostics without making the result incomplete. Add a typed inventory snapshot containing records, revisions, page hashes, provenance, effective-head diagnostics, and an explicit completeness state; require the gate to fail closed on races, overflow, decode errors, or unstable reads.

suggestions.title: Do not expose partially published approval batches
suggestions.rationale: `BaseWikiStore` exposes per-page CAS, while SQLite implements CAS for one page at a time; there is no cross-record transaction in the shared store contract. Publishing multiple entries and then projecting edges can expose a half-approved proposal. Use a commit-manifest/approval-batch record that readers require before considering entries effective, or add a backend-wide transactional batch contract and parity-test it.

suggestions.title: Version the envelope and relation vocabulary explicitly
suggestions.rationale: `DecisionRecord.schema_version` is `Literal[1]`, `codec.py` accepts only `parrot-adr:v1`, and `DecisionLink.relation` is closed to `explains`, `supported_by`, and `supersedes`. Adding `about`, `targets`, `contradicts`, approval metadata, or batch state cannot be safely handled as optional fields. Implement versioned decode adapters, a new envelope marker, explicit legacy-read/new-write policy, and deterministic rejection by old writers/readers.

suggestions.title: Separate effective-governing inventory from ordinary retrieval
suggestions.rationale: `DecisionService._visible()` returns most documented records, including unknown or proposed source statuses, while `why()` merely ranks accepted records first. Supersession is not evaluated there, and `review.py` appends a supersedes link without validating active heads, cycles, or target equivalence. Build an effective-head validator before dossier or gate evaluation; do not reuse `why()`/`for_symbol()` output as gate input.

suggestions.title: Add a typed target resolver instead of interpreting empty structural results
suggestions.rationale: `StructuralService.outline()` returns an empty result for invalid, missing, excluded, or unindexed paths, and `lookup()` is explicitly a ranked suggestion API. The current service has no directory inventory/completeness result, while `_is_confined()` uses default exclusions rather than proving the configured scan inventory. A gate resolver should return distinct resolved, missing, unsupported, stale, and incomplete states for exact `sym:`, `file:`, and `dir:` targets.

suggestions.title: Treat blast-radius truncation and read-repair as audit incompleteness
suggestions.rationale: `blast_radius()` is bounded by depth and a 500-node cap, skips dangling nodes, and reports only a boolean `truncated`; structural queries may also rescan and mutate the wiki plane through `_ensure_fresh()`. Using this result as a complete approval radius can produce false-clean audits. The gate needs a read-only structural snapshot with scan coverage, freshness, lock, dangling-node, and truncation diagnostics, and must downgrade or block incomplete evaluations.

suggestions.title: Make the `about` taxonomy independent from free-form SDD tags
suggestions.rationale: `DocTaxonomy` deliberately permits arbitrary normalized tags and only warns for unknown projects, so silently mapping every tag to an authoritative subsystem concept would change existing SDD semantics. The OKF vocabulary already contains stable `about`, `contradicts`, `supersedes`, and `supported_by` relation values. Introduce a versioned decision-taxonomy mapping with explicit unknown/unmapped diagnostics, and use existing relation strings only for rebuildable projections.

suggestions.title: Keep the spec-entry parser separate from legacy ADR refresh and define revision transitions
suggestions.rationale: `parse_adr()` produces one path-identified record, uses path hashing for identity, and intentionally ignores unsupported frontmatter keys; `refresh_decisions()` reconstructs records and persists them through the ordinary per-record path. A spec producer must have a separate strict parser for multi-entry YAML, stable document/entry IDs, intra-batch references, and previous-revision pins, while preserving legacy ADR behavior and never resetting history through refresh.

suggestions.title: Make approval an executable SDD transition
suggestions.rationale: The current `/sdd-spec` instructions scaffold and commit a spec, then tell the maintainer to mark status approved and run `/sdd-task`; `sdd/templates/spec.md` has no machine-defined Decisions/Consequences contract. The named `scripts/sdd/check_spec_consequences.py` surface is absent from the repository. Add one shared checker following the existing report pattern, and make the approval/task entry point refuse status transition or task decomposition unless the check is complete and blocking findings are resolved.

suggestions.title: Freeze the approval-evidence trust adapter before implementing ingestion
suggestions.rationale: `ReviewEvent.actor` is caller-provided and `DecisionService.review()` accepts it without verifying authority, scope, or an external approval reference. The design correctly says there is no fallback to trusting `status: approved`, but the exploration lists no open question for choosing the adapter. Either specify a verifiable approval source before implementation or limit v1 to preview/evaluation and reject publication and waivers.

suggestions.title: Require backend and transport parity for the new evaluation API
suggestions.rationale: Decision operations and MCP transport are registered through separate operation descriptors and dispatch branches, while existing parity tests make SQLite and memory mandatory and report live-backend gaps explicitly. Add consequence-evaluation parity tests for SQLite and memory, configured live backends, CLI/MCP JSON equivalence, offline zero-LLM behavior, snapshot incompleteness, strict parser failures, supersession races, and manifest publication.
